# e2e scripts whose ONLY coverage reads their SOURCE and asserts on its TEXT.
#
# Graded by scripts/check-e2e-execution-coverage.py (bd-e2d1q). Format:
#
#     <script> | <covering test> | <what execution coverage is absent>
#
# THIS IS NOT AN IGNORE-LIST, and the distinction is mechanical rather than
# aspirational. Every entry is RE-EARNED on each run, the same way
# retired.txt is re-earned by scripts/e2e_invocation_audit.sh:
#
#   * the script must still be executed by NOTHING. The moment anything runs
#     it, this line is RED and must be deleted -- so the file can only shrink.
#   * the covering test must EXIST and must really reference the script. A
#     line naming a test that was renamed away is RED, not silently ignored.
#   * the script must not also sit in orphan_baseline.txt (un-referenced) or
#     retired.txt (covered elsewhere); either would contradict this claim.
#   * the third field must be non-empty. An entry that does not say what is
#     unproven is doing the opposite of its job.
#
# WHY THE CLASS IS WORTH TRACKING AT ALL. A source-conformance test is a real
# job -- a text scan is the right tool for a cross-cutting logging contract,
# and eight of these enforce the J1 contract across the graph suite. The defect
# is that it OCCUPIES THE SLOT a runner would occupy and reports green either
# way, while `e2e_invocation_audit.sh` counts the script wired because it IS
# referenced. A reader who greps the name finds `tests/..._e2e_contract.rs`
# and reasonably concludes it is covered.
#
# TWENTY, NOT EIGHTEEN. bd-e2d1q enumerated 18 and measured its population as
# "e2e scripts reachable ONLY from tests/**". That filter excluded two scripts
# on the strength of references that execute nothing:
#
#   auto_enroll_perf_gate.sh   scripts/bench.sh:1403 prints its name in an
#                              `echo ... >&2` message, plus one README line.
#                              It sits in the SAME five-entry const array as
#                              four scripts the bead does list.
#   host_calibration.sh        named in src/core/profile.rs and
#                              src/core/budget_delta_recommender.rs as a
#                              repair-hint STRING (`repair: Some("rch exec --
#                              scripts/...")`), and in docs/degraded_codes.md
#                              as prose.
#
# Both exclusions are the mention-versus-invocation error the bead is about,
# committed by the bead's own population filter. Re-measured 2026-11-09.

scripts/e2e_incremental_index.sh | tests/contracts/index_intake_schema.rs | intake schema text asserted; the incremental index path is never driven
